title: An unexpected listener
briefing: A security scan of net-01 came back dirty: something is listening on a port
that shouldn't be open. Known-good services are ssh (22), the web server
(80) and the app (8080). Anything else is suspicious.
tips: `ss -tlnp` lists every listening TCP port and the process behind it.
One port stands out — and its process isn't a normal service.
objective: Find the port the rogue backdoor is listening on, and write just that port number to ~/finding.txt.
expert_objective: Identify the backdoor's listening port; record the number in ~/finding.txt.
hints: List listeners with owners: `ss -tlnp`. Compare against 22/80/8080.
There's a 'nc' (netcat) process listening — that's the backdoor. Note its port.
The odd one out is port 4444 (process nc). `echo 4444 > ~/finding.txt`.
explanation: `ss -tlnp` is the fastest way to answer 'what is this box exposing to the network?'. A listener you can't account for — here a netcat shell on 4444 — is a classic backdoor. Enumerate the expected ports, and whatever's left is your lead.
